title: Supply Chain Wars
description: A chess-inspired strategy game where you control global trade routes and supply chains. Deploy your HQ Warehouse, Fleet Commander, Cargo Ships, Air Freight, Delivery Drones, and Trucks to dominate logistics corridors. Secure ports, factories, and distribution centers to build an unstoppable supply network and outmaneuver the competition.
learning_objectives: Develop strategic thinking by planning multi-step logistics maneuvers across trade routes
Practice resource allocation by deciding where to deploy limited fleet and freight assets
Understand supply chain tradeoffs when choosing between speed, cost, and territorial control
Build spatial reasoning skills through positional control of key logistics hubs
Learn adaptive decision-making by responding to the opponent's shifting supply chain strategy
Cultivate systems thinking by managing interconnected nodes in a global distribution network
how_to_play: Each turn you get 2 Action Points (AP). Moving a piece costs 1 AP, and using a special ability costs 1 AP.
Pieces move like chess: Warehouse=King, Fleet=Queen, Cargo=Rook, Air Freight=Bishop, Delivery Drone=Knight, Truck=Pawn.
Capture enemy pieces by moving onto their square. Trucks promote to Fleet Commander when reaching the last row.
Control resource tiles (Ports, Factories, etc.) by placing your pieces on them. Each tile generates income per turn.
Win by: capturing the enemy HQ Warehouse, controlling 3+ resource tiles, or reaching $10M in trade revenue.
Use each piece's unique abilities strategically — the Delivery Drone's rapid deployment and the Air Freight's route swapping can dominate any supply corridor.
objectives: Capture the rival HQ Warehouse for an instant logistics monopoly victory
Control 3 or more key supply hubs for a trade route domination win
Build your trade revenue to $10 million through strategic supply chain control

storybook_pages.title: The Global Supply Chain Showdown
storybook_pages.text: Two rival logistics empires face off for control of the world's most valuable trade routes. Your fleet of cargo ships, delivery drones, and freight carriers must outmaneuver the competition across contested supply corridors. Every shipment counts — margins are razor-thin and dominance belongs to the most efficient operator.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: two rival logistics companies facing each other across a world map styled as a chess board, cargo ships and drones, ports and factories glowing, dramatic ocean and sky, digital illustration style

storybook_pages.title: Your Logistics Fleet
storybook_pages.text:
HQ Warehouse (King) — Your headquarters, protect at all costs.
Fleet Commander (Queen) — Most powerful, moves any direction.
Cargo Ship (Rook) — Straight-line shipping lane specialist.
Air Freight (Bishop) — Diagonal air corridor navigator.
Delivery Drone (Knight) — L-shaped rapid deployment unit.
Truck (Pawn) — Ground transport, promotes to Fleet Commander!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: diverse logistics fleet as chess pieces on a cargo port, warehouse as king, drone as knight, truck as pawn, colorful modern illustration, game character design with shipping and logistics theme

storybook_pages.title: The Trade Route Map
storybook_pages.text: The 8x8 board represents contested global trade territory with 6 key logistics hubs: Ports, Factories, Distribution Centers, Rail Hubs, Airports, and Markets. Control them to generate trade revenue each turn and build your supply chain empire!
storybook_pages.image_prompt: birds eye view of a colorful 8x8 game board with glowing logistics hub tiles, shipping containers and cargo cranes, global trade map style with routes connecting nodes, digital game art

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.
